brief.greeting: Good morning. The internet swapped LLM voices while Linux quietly shipped another prepatch.

stories.headline: Chat templates give LLMs a self‑referential twist
stories.body: **Self‑referential mode activated:** A new chat template forces large language models to talk about themselves, turning every reply into a meta‑commentary. The change is already being discussed on Hacker News.
stories.why: If you build AI assistants, expect a quirky edge case in prompt handling.

stories.headline: Linux 7.3‑rc5 lands with no red flags
stories.body: **No surprises this time:** The latest 7.3‑rc5 prepatch is out for testing, and Linus Torvalds reports a clean bill of health. Developers can start poking around without fearing a surprise regression.
stories.why: A stable kernel base lets you ship drivers and firmware updates faster.

stories.headline: 8‑billion‑parameter Contrastive‑LM hits Hugging Face
stories.body: **Big model, modest uptake:** Contrastive‑LM/CLM‑v0.1‑8B is now available, packing 8 B parameters. It has already seen 766 downloads and 434 likes on the platform.
stories.why: Engineers can experiment with a sizable open model without the cost of training one from scratch.

quick_hits.text: **Cheatsheet:** navi offers an interactive CLI reference for common commands.
**Books:** free‑programming‑books curates thousands of free coding texts.
**IR hack:** A pocket‑sized computer powers an IR blaster for remote control.
**Lawn mower:** A repurposed irrigation pivot now trims grass automatically.
**Flip‑dot art:** A fluid simulation runs on a low‑res flip‑dot board at EMF 2026.

brief.sign_off: Catch you tomorrow, and keep those compilers warm.

highlights.title: "As a Language Model": Chat Template Switches LLM Self-Referential Voice
highlights.summary: A new chat template changes large language models to speak in a self-referential voice.
highlights.detail: The template swaps the system prompt so the model refers to itself as "I" and describes its own capabilities. This alteration is primarily a prompt engineering trick, not a model architecture change, and can be applied to any compatible LLM.

highlights.title: Kernel prepatch 7.3-rc5
highlights.summary: The Linux 7.3‑rc5 kernel prepatch has been released for testing, with Linus Torvalds noting no alarming changes.
highlights.detail: Although the diffstat appears large, the changes are described as routine updates rather than major new features. Developers are encouraged to test the prepatch to catch regressions before the final 7.3 release.

highlights.title: denisidoro/navi
highlights.summary: The GitHub project denisidoro/navi provides an interactive command‑line cheatsheet for quick reference to common commands.
highlights.detail: Implemented in Rust, the tool parses user queries and displays concise examples, aiming to reduce context‑switching for developers. It supports extensible plugins and can be integrated into shell workflows.

highlights.title: EbookFoundation/free-programming-books
highlights.summary: EbookFoundation/free-programming-books is a curated list of freely available programming books across many languages and topics.
highlights.detail: The repository aggregates links to PDFs, online editions, and open‑source textbooks, regularly updated by contributors. It serves as a central resource for self‑learners and educators seeking no‑cost learning material.

highlights.title: InfinityLoop1308/PipePipe
highlights.summary: InfinityLoop1308/PipePipe is an open‑source Android application that enables unrestricted browsing of YouTube and other streaming services.
highlights.detail: The app bypasses platform restrictions by using custom playback pipelines and supports ad‑free viewing. It is distributed under an MIT license and encourages community contributions for additional service integrations.

items.title: Model: Contrastive-LM/CLM-v0.1-8B
items.summary: Contrastive-LM/CLM-v0.1-8B, an 8‑billion‑parameter language model, is now available on Hugging Face.
items.detail: The model is optimized for text‑ranking tasks and has attracted moderate community interest. Its release adds another large‑scale option for developers needing contrastive learning without fine‑tuning a full‑size model.

items.title: Model: XingChen-AGI/TeleOCR
items.summary: XingChen-AGI/TeleOCR, an image‑to‑text model, is trending on Hugging Face with strong download numbers.
items.detail: TeleOCR converts photographed text into digital strings, targeting OCR use cases where traditional pipelines struggle. Its popularity suggests a demand for ready‑to‑use vision‑language models in the community.

items.title: An IR Blaster Project, in a Nutshell
items.summary: A hackathon project demonstrates an IR blaster built from a pocket‑sized computer.
items.detail: The device can transmit infrared signals to control consumer electronics, showcasing how modern microcontrollers can replace legacy remote‑control hardware. The build highlights the rapid miniaturization of computing platforms.

items.title: Center-Pivot System Modified to Mow Lawn
items.summary: An existing center‑pivot irrigation system has been repurposed to mow lawns automatically.
items.detail: The modification attaches a cutting mechanism to the rotating arm, turning a large‑scale agricultural device into a novel autonomous mower. This illustrates creative reuse of infrastructure for unconventional tasks.

items.title: Defeating Satellite Spoofing with Galileo’s Encryption
items.summary: Hackaday reports that satellite navigation systems, despite their critical role in navigation and timekeeping, remain vulnerable to attacks such as jamming and spoofing.
items.detail: The article outlines various threat vectors affecting GNSS constellations and highlights the need for stronger cryptographic protections. It references ongoing research into authentication mechanisms but notes implementation challenges across legacy hardware.

items.title: Enormous Fluid Simulation on Flip Dots is also Enormous Amount of Work
items.summary: A fluid simulation displayed on a flip‑dot board was showcased at EMF 2026, demonstrating large‑scale visual computing on low‑resolution hardware.
items.detail: The project, created by mitxela, required extensive custom driver work and real‑time rendering optimizations to drive thousands of electromechanical dots. It serves as a proof‑of‑concept for artistic installations that blend classic display tech with modern simulation algorithms.

items.title: Going on a Tangent with the Intel 8087’s Hybrid CORDIC Algorithm
items.summary: Ken Shirriff and collaborators reverse‑engineered the Intel 8087 FPU’s hybrid CORDIC implementation of the FPTAN instruction.
items.detail: Their analysis reveals how the 8087 combines lookup tables with iterative rotations to compute tangent values efficiently on early microprocessors. The findings shed light on historical design trade‑offs between accuracy and silicon cost, informing modern low‑power arithmetic unit designs.

items.title: The412Banner/winlator-contents
items.summary: The winlator-contents repository provides a component catalog index for BannerHub and Winlator clients, hosting a contents.json that mirrors nightlies_components.json, while the actual component binaries are stored in The412Banner/Nightlies releases.
items.detail: This repository acts as a lightweight reference point, allowing clients to retrieve up-to-date component listings without bundling large binaries. It simplifies version synchronization between the client applications and the nightly build artifacts.

items.title: bevyengine/bevy
items.summary: Bevy is an open-source, data-driven game engine written in Rust, emphasizing simplicity and modularity.
items.detail: The engine leverages Rust's safety guarantees and a ECS (Entity Component System) architecture to enable fast iteration. Its design targets both 2D and 3D development while maintaining a minimal API surface.

items.title: cataclysmbn/Cataclysm-BN
items.summary: Cataclysm: Bright Nights is a fork of Cataclysm:DDA that adds a dedicated mod registry hosted at https://mods.cataclysmbn.org/.
items.detail: The project maintains compatibility with the original game's mechanics while providing a streamlined way for players to discover and install community mods. It aims to foster a more active modding ecosystem compared to the upstream version.
